sm05-en-full.title: Survival Mode: You vs the Sun ☀️ Colosseum, Chand Baori, Louvre, Maraya
sm05-en-full.desc:
No shade. No rain. No air conditioning. Four levels, four bosses made of sunshine, and you beat them with sails, stairs, stars and mirrors.

0:00 No shade. No rain. No air conditioning.
0:13 Level 1: the Colosseum vs the Roman summer
1:18 Level 2: Chand Baori vs the dry season
2:19 Level 3: the Louvre Abu Dhabi vs the frying pan
3:23 Final level: Maraya vs the oven
4:24 Results

Every level is a real build: the Colosseum pulled a roof of sails over fifty thousand people on two hundred and forty wooden poles, Chand Baori takes thirty-five hundred steps down to water where it is about five degrees cooler, the Louvre Abu Dhabi's dome is a hundred and eighty meters wide and woven from seven thousand eight hundred and fifty metal stars, and Maraya wears almost ten thousand square meters of mirror that bounce most of the desert sun back to the sky.

New episode every day. Subscribe, or the boss wins.
#engineering #survival #howitworks

ep89-noor-en.title: Noor Ouarzazate: Solar Power After Dark ☀️
ep89-noor-en.desc:
A solar plant that keeps making power after the sun goes down. ☀️
About seven thousand mirrors aim sunlight at a 247 m tower that heats molten salt past 500 C. The hot salt waits in tanks and runs the turbines for hours after dark.
Would you visit it? 👇

How it works: Noor Ouarzazate in Morocco aims mirrors at a 247 m tower that heats molten salt which keeps the turbines running after dark

ep90-pen-en.title: Ballpoint Pen: A Tiny Ball That Rolls Out the Ink ✒️
ep90-pen-en.desc:
The pen in your pocket writes with a tiny rolling ball. ✒️
A steel or tungsten carbide ball sits in a brass tip and rolls thick, fast-drying ink onto the page, and a tiny hole in the barrel lets air in so the ink keeps flowing.
Do you still click yours when you think? 👇

How a ballpoint pen works: a tiny ball in a socket at the tip rolls thick, fast-drying ink onto the paper, and a small hole in the barrel lets air in so the ink keeps flowing.

ep76-cooker-en.title: Pressure Cooker: Water Hotter Than Boiling 🍲
ep76-cooker-en.desc:
A pot that gets water hotter than boiling, and cooks beans in minutes. 🍲
Lock the lid and the trapped steam raises the pressure, so the water boils at about 120°C instead of 100°C. A little weight lets the extra steam out (that's the whistle), a backup plug melts if the vent clogs, and a pin keeps the lid locked until the pressure is gone.
How many whistles for your lentils? 👇
Next build: the Golden Gate Bridge 🌉 Subscribe so you don't miss it.

How a pressure cooker works: the sealed lid traps steam, the pressure rises, and water boils at about 120 °C instead of 100 °C, so food cooks much faster, even high in the mountains where water boils cooler. A weighted valve lets extra steam out (the whistle), a safety plug melts if the vent clogs, and a locking pin keeps the lid shut until the pressure is gone.

#pressurecooker #cooking #howitworks #Shorts

ep91-arch-en.title: Gateway Arch: How Two Legs Met 192 m Up 🏙️
ep91-arch-en.desc:
Two steel legs leaning toward each other, with nothing in between. 🏙️
The Gateway Arch in St. Louis was built double-walled, with concrete between the walls, using cranes that climbed the legs. On the last morning the sun heated one leg, so it was sprayed with cold water and jacked apart to fit the final piece.
Would you ride the pods to the top? 👇
Next build: a car seatbelt 🚗 Subscribe so you don't miss it.

How the Gateway Arch was built: the 192 m stainless steel arch in St. Louis was built as two leaning legs with climbing cranes. A truss braced them, and on the last day the sun heated one leg, so it was cooled with water and jacked apart to fit the final piece in 1965.

#gatewayarch #stlouis #engineering #Shorts

ep77-goldengate-en.title: Golden Gate Bridge: Its Orange Was the Undercoat 🌉
ep77-goldengate-en.desc:
The Golden Gate's famous orange started out as the undercoat. 🌉
The steel arrived in a reddish primer, and architect Irving Morrow kept the color because it stands out in the fog (the Navy wanted black and yellow stripes). The south tower was built inside a concrete tub in the open sea, each main cable is spun from 27,572 wires, and a safety net under the deck saved 19 workers.
Have you walked across it? 👇
Next build: the Gateway Arch 🌈 Subscribe so you don't miss it.

How the Golden Gate Bridge was built: opened in 1937 across a strait with strong tides, ocean swells and fog, its south tower stands in the open sea, built inside a concrete fender that was pumped dry. Its International Orange came from the red primer on the steel and stays visible in fog. Two main cables of 27,572 wires each carry the deck, and a safety net under it saved 19 workers, the Halfway to Hell Club. About 200,000 people walked across on opening day.

#goldengatebridge #sanfrancisco #engineering #Shorts

ep92-seatbelt-en.title: Seatbelt: The Tiny Pendulum That Locks It 🚗
ep92-seatbelt-en.desc:
The belt across your chest does one trick: it locks when you need it. 🚗
Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin added the chest strap in 1959 and Volvo gave the patent away. Inside, a spring-loaded spool stays loose until a tiny pendulum swings in a hard stop and a catch locks it, and a tiny charge pulls the buckle down to remove slack.
Do you click it without thinking? 👇
Next build: a bridge 625 m above a canyon 🌉 Subscribe so you don't miss it.

How a seatbelt works: the three-point belt was developed by Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin in 1959. A spring-loaded spool stays loose until a weighted pendulum swings in a sudden stop and a catch locks it, and a pretensioner pulls the buckle down to remove slack.

#seatbelt #cars #howitworks #Shorts
